source.title: 12. Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes. 12. Retinopathy, neuropathy, and foot care: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl. 1):S261–S276.

guideline_boundary: Recommendations are panel/guideline statements represented with author_conclusion plus guideline_recommendation tags. Quantitative effects from underlying studies are tagged secondary_reported_result and remain anchored to this Standards chapter rather than being represented as primary-study enrollment by the ADA chapter.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no guideline_recommendation atom kind, so formal recommendations use author_conclusion with descriptive tags.
ADA recommendation evidence grades are stored in tags because the schema has no dedicated grade field.

Some clinically important secondary evidence lacks enough source-reported context for a defensible quantitative_result object and is therefore preserved as narrative atoms rather than forcing missing fields.
extraction_limitations: The full ADA guideline-development methodology and evidence-grade definitions are in the separate Introduction and Methodology and are not part of dc26s012.pdf.
Bibliography entries are not atomized; all 169 are preserved in the reference task queue.
All atoms remain needs_review because this run does not represent independent human verification.
No external current-practice or regulatory verification was performed because the user requested processing of the supplied source and did not activate @VERIFY.
protocol_version_note: The project file is named summary-evaluation-appraisal-protocol-v4-compact.md, while its internal heading identifies Integrated Compact v3. The v4-named project source was treated as governing and the naming mismatch was recorded rather than silently reconciled.
